title: Library nomenclature and constraint simplification for control atoms
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary: The Figma library contains a set of low-level control atoms (buttons, inputs, icon buttons, small tables and chart primitives) with inconsistent naming, deeply nested variant trees, and mixed constraint settings that cause layout regressions when instances are resized or when token values change. This ticket scopes a focused, low-risk pass to: 1) standardize naming to a stable semantic schema; 2) flatten variant axes to make switching predictable; 3) simplify auto-layout constraints to preserve density across container resizing; 4) re-map local tokens to the canonical semantic token set and publish a gated release checklist.

Why now: Multiple engineering teams have reported breakages during runtime UI experiments when token names changed, and platform QA found several instances that break layout at small widths. Fixing the atomic primitives reduces churn across hundreds of composited instances in product files and improves publish reliability.

Out of scope: full refactor of complex composed components (datagrids, complex chart compositions) — this ticket focuses on atoms and lightweight primitives that are reused widely.

Figma files: Primary library: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/Redwood-Atoms-Library (internal). PRD: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3c_PRD_refactor. Engineering implementation notes and rollout plan: https://github.com/redwood-inference/design-system/issues/412

Owner: Design (Diego) with cross-team review from Platform UX (Ava), iOS (Rina Patel), Web Eng (Marcus Li).
acceptance_criteria: All atomic button variants follow naming: <semantic>-<size>-<state> (e.g., primary-md-default)
Variant sets for buttons/inputs/icon-buttons are flattened to max 2 axes (size, state) with <= 8 total permutations
Auto-layout constraints on atoms use pinning rules that preserve internal spacing when instances are resized (no clipped icons or truncated labels at 320px min container)
All local color/spacing/token references are mapped to canonical semantic tokens (colors.text.primary, spacing.2, etc.) and no duplicate token names remain in the library file
Publish checklist completed and gated publish performed with rollback notes; no downstream instances throw missing token errors
Design review approved and engineering implementation task created with observable regression test checklist
tasks: Inventory: run token and component usage export for atoms (scripted Figma plugin) and capture top 150 instances
Naming: apply semantic rename map to all atoms, add README page in the file describing schema
Variants: collapse multi-axis variant trees into size x state; move deprecated permutations to a hidden 'legacy' page
Auto-layout: update frame constraints for icons, labels and paddings; add min-width test instances (320, 360, 768)
Tokens: swap local color/spacing tokens for design-system semantic tokens and update token aliases
Accessibility: ensure focus outlines and hit target sizes meet 44px min area for tappable atoms
Publish: run publish with CI gating, note breaking changes and update library changelog
Post-publish: monitor usage dashboards and tag any regressions for quick rollback
decisions: Adopt semantic naming instead of BEM-like or platform-specific prefixes to reduce cross-platform diffs
Keep legacy permutations on a hidden page rather than deleting for a 2-release window to ease migration
Limit variant axes to two to keep the UI for switching states intuitive for engineers and PMs
Use a single canonical token file (tokens.sem.json) as the source of truth; do not create file-local color tokens
Gate the publish with a staged rollout: design smoke tests -> small product teams -> full publish
